title: Capture handshake, stream quiescence detection, and kernel negotiation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Improve reliability of multi-stream capture/replay by adding an explicit capture handshake, detecting stream quiescence windows before capture, and negotiating a kernel capability table to choose safe fallbacks at replay time. The goal is to reduce non-deterministic replay failures and expensive global recaptures while keeping latency and throughput targets intact.
background: We've seen intermittent replay mismatches when concurrent prefill and decode streams race to capture CUDA Graph segments. Existing mitigations (coarse fences and full recapture) are expensive or cause latency spikes under burst traffic. This ticket prototypes a coordination protocol that lets streams declare quiescent epochs, exchange lightweight capability info (kernel features and sequence-length bounds), and do verified speculative captures with a cheap checksum validation before committing a shared graph.
success_criteria: Reduce replay_failure_rate (observed in canary) to < 0.5% for workloads with 8+ concurrent streams
Avoid full recapture in > 95% of transient kernel-mismatch incidents; use targeted micro-recapture instead
End-to-end p95 latency increase due to handshake < 1.5ms for typical 128-token prompts
Add telemetry that shows handshake success rate and average quiescence wait time
technical_design:
Design doc: https://confluence.internal.redwood/runtime/capture-handshake-protocol (draft). Core ideas:
- Capture handshake: producer stream emits CAPTURE_INTENT with epoch id, expected seq-length window, and kernel feature bitmap. Consumer streams acknowledge readiness or return NACK with reason code.
- Stream quiescence detection: measure token-generation inter-arrival times; if stream is in low activity for configured window (quiesce_ms) we allow capture.
- Kernel negotiation table: runtime maintains a per-device capability vector negotiated at startup and verified during capture; when mismatch occurs use a predefined fallback kernel with binary compatibility.
- Speculative capture + checksum: after capture, compute lightweight kernel-rendered checksum on first few tokens; if checksum matches across streams commit graph, otherwise trigger micro-recapture limited to affected nodes.
- Fallthrough: if negotiation fails, fall back to single-stream kernels for affected streams and emit alert.
Link to prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/proto-capture-handshake (PR: #1526)
implementation_notes: Add CAPTURE_INTENT and CAPTURE_ACK RPCs to stream control plane (proto changes in pr-1526)
Quiescence detection uses EWMA of inter-token latency with configurable threshold; default quiesce_ms=8ms
Store kernel capability bitmap in device metadata; add validation at graph-build time
Implement checksum as XOR64 of first N (default 16) output token embeddings post-capture to keep cost low
Micro-recapture should only re-run kernels for affected attention blocks; reuse existing graph segments where possible
test_plan: Unit tests for handshake RPCs and capability bitmap parsing
Synthetic load test: 64 streams, mix of prefill/decode; measure handshake success and replay mismatches
Canary in us-west-2 with 10% traffic for runtime-1.22; monitor for regressions for 48h
Fault injection: simulate kernel capability flip during capture and verify micro-recapture path
Integration test to assert no deadlocks when two streams race to capture same segment
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.capture_handshake.enabled=false by default
Merge prototype to canary branch and run synthetic tests (QA)
Enable flag for 10% of traffic in staging for 24h, then 10% in canary prod for 48h
If metrics pass, increase to 50% then 100% over two days with monitoring windows
If replay_failure_rate > 1% at any window, rollback flag immediately and collect traces
risks: Handshake adds coordination latency; may increase p99 under extreme burst patterns
Checksum heuristic could produce false positives for minor non-determinism -> unnecessary micro-recaptures
Incorrect capability bitmap definitions across driver versions may cause repeated fallbacks
Edge-case deadlocks if ACK/NACK paths aren't idempotent under retry
